body:
The development of modern poetic forms

Modern Gujarati poetry developed new literary forms through interaction with Sanskrit poetic traditions, English literature and changing ideas about individual experience. Two important forms are Khandakavya and the sonnet.

While Khandakavya combines narrative and emotional expression around a significant incident, the sonnet expresses a developed thought or feeling within a prescribed number of lines.

Khandakavya

A Khandakavya is a relatively short narrative poem centred on a significant incident, situation or portion of a larger story, presenting it as an emotionally complete poetic composition.

The word Khanda means a part or portion, while Kavya means poetry. Unlike a Mahakavya or extensive epic poem, a Khandakavya does not normally attempt to narrate the entire life of a hero or a long sequence of historical events.

It selects a particular event or decisive moment and develops its emotional significance through characters, circumstances and poetic expression.

Principal characteristics

  • It concentrates on a limited but significant incident.
  • It combines narrative development with emotional expression.
  • Its subject may be drawn from mythology, history or imagination.
  • It normally forms a complete poetic composition despite its limited subject matter.
  • It does not have a fixed requirement of 14 lines or any other universal line count.

Kavi Kant

Manishankar Ratnaji Bhatt, popularly known by his pen name Kant, established Khandakavya as a distinctive form of modern Gujarati poetry.

His compositions combined elements of Sanskrit and Western poetic traditions. His narrative poems became important models for subsequent Gujarati writers of Khandakavya.

Work by KantPrincipal subject
Vasant VijayA decisive episode in the life of Pandu
AtijnanThe predicament of Sahadeva
Chakravak MithunSeparation and suffering of a pair of birds
DevayaniA subject drawn from mythology

Vasant Vijay is one of the best-known examples of Gujarati Khandakavya. The poem concentrates on a significant episode involving Pandu rather than retelling the entire Mahabharata.

Other poets, including Kalapi, also contributed to this literary form. Kalapi's Bilvamangal is another example of Gujarati Khandakavya.

A Khandakavya may narrate only part of a larger story, but it is not necessarily an unfinished poem. Its selected incident is developed into an independent composition.

Sonnet

A sonnet is a traditionally 14-line poem that develops a central thought, emotion or experience, usually incorporating a significant turn in its development.

The sonnet originated in Italian literature and entered Gujarati poetry through the influence of English literature. It is therefore distinct from the older indigenous forms of medieval Gujarati verse.

Structural features

The sonnet has several established structural patterns. Two of the most important are the Petrarchan and Shakespearean forms.

  • Petrarchan or Italian sonnet: An octave of 8 lines followed by a sestet of 6 lines.
  • Shakespearean or English sonnet: 3 quatrains of 4 lines each followed by a concluding couplet of 2 lines.

Both structures contain a total of 14 lines. They differ in the grouping of those lines and the manner in which the central thought is developed.

A significant change in thought, argument or emotional perspective is commonly called a Volta. In a traditional Petrarchan sonnet, this turn often occurs between the octave and sestet.

Gujarati poets adapted different sonnet structures to suit the language. Consequently, not every Gujarati sonnet follows an identical division or rhyme pattern.

Balwantray Kalyanray Thakore

Balwantray Kalyanray Thakore, commonly referred to as B. K. Thakore, is recognised as a pioneering exponent of the Gujarati sonnet.

His poem Bhanakara, composed in 1888, is widely recognised as the first artistically accomplished Gujarati sonnet.

His collection Mharan Sonnet, first published in 1935, is an important contribution to the development of Gujarati sonnet poetry.

Khandakavya and sonnet compared

FeatureKhandakavyaSonnet
Central principleSignificant narrative incidentDeveloped thought or emotion
LengthVariable14 lines
Major Gujarati pioneerKavi KantB. K. Thakore
Representative exampleVasant VijayBhanakara

Prelims focus

  • Kavi Kant was the major pioneer of modern Gujarati Khandakavya.
  • Vasant Vijay, Atijnan and Chakravak Mithun are works by Kant.
  • A sonnet traditionally contains 14 lines.
  • Italian sonnet: 8 lines followed by 6 lines.
  • B. K. Thakore composed Bhanakara in 1888.
  • Trap: Khandakavya has no mandatory 14-line structure.

[References: Gujarati Vishwakosh, entries Khandakavya, Kant, Sonnet, Thakore, Balwantray Kalyanray, and Mharan Sonnet. Online references consulted 26 November 2026.]

title: Khandakavya and Sonnet: Modern Gujarati Poetic Forms

body:
Identifying a literary form

The major Gujarati literary forms can be distinguished by considering what each composition primarily attempts to achieve. Some narrate stories, some communicate devotional feelings, some accompany social occasions and others follow a prescribed poetic structure.

These categories are useful for identification, although they are not completely exclusive. For example, an Akhyan may express devotion while narrating a story, and a Garbi may belong to the wider tradition of Pad poetry.

Narrative literary forms

Rasa is an early narrative poetic tradition extensively developed by Jain authors. Its representative work is Shalibhadrasuri's Bharateshwar Bahubali Rasa, composed in 1185 CE.

Akhyan develops a connected story through successive episodes or Kadavu units. Bhalan is traditionally recognised as its father, while Premanand brought the form to maturity. Premanand's Sudamacharitra is a representative example.

Khandakavya is a modern narrative poem concentrating on a significant incident rather than presenting an extensive story. Kavi Kant's Vasant Vijay is a representative example.

Lyrical and devotional literary forms

Pad is a broad category of short, singable lyrical poetry. Narsinh Mehta's Vaishnav Jan To Tene Kahiye is a famous example.

Prabhatiyu is identified by its traditional association with early-morning devotional singing. Narsinh Mehta's Jag Ne Jadava is a representative example.

Garbi is particularly associated with Krishna devotion and the expression of divine love. Dayaram's Shyam Rang Samipe Na Javu is a well-known example.

Occasion-based folk literature

Fatana express humour and playful teasing during weddings. Gharma Noti Khand is an example from the oral wedding-song tradition.

Marasiya express mourning and remembrance. Satan-Visal Sambhare, preserved in Jhaverchand Meghani's Ritugeeto, represents this tradition.

Poetry with a prescribed line count

The sonnet traditionally contains 14 lines and develops a central thought or feeling. B. K. Thakore's Bhanakara, composed in 1888, is a pioneering Gujarati example.

Important literary associations

PersonalityLiterary formRepresentative work
ShalibhadrasuriRasaBharateshwar Bahubali Rasa

Narsinh MehtaPrabhatiyuJag Ne Jadava

Kavi KantKhandakavyaVasant Vijay
B. K. ThakoreSonnetBhanakara

Jhaverchand Meghani holds a different position in the folk-song tradition. His contribution includes collecting, editing and preserving oral literature. Chundadi preserves Gujarati wedding songs, while Ritugeeto includes examples of Marasiya expressing remembrance through descriptions of seasons.

Distinctions that prevent common errors

  • Bhalan and Premanand: Both are associated with Akhyan, but Bhalan is traditionally called its father and Premanand represents its mature development.
  • Pad and Prabhatiyu: Pad is the broader lyrical category; Prabhatiyu has a particular association with the morning.
  • Garbi and Garbo: Krishna devotion and Shakti worship are their respective characteristic literary associations, without constituting absolute subject restrictions.
  • Fatana and Marasiya: The first expresses wedding humour; the second expresses grief and remembrance.
  • Akhyan and Khandakavya: Akhyan generally develops an extended story through successive episodes; Khandakavya focuses on a significant incident as an independent poem.
  • Khandakavya and sonnet: Khandakavya is identified primarily through its narrative subject; a sonnet is identified through its traditional 14-line structure and development of thought or feeling.

One-glance revision

[References: GCERT, Class 7 Social Science, Gujarati medium, Chapters 7 and 8, sections on Gujarati Bhakti poets and Gujarati literature; GCERT, Class 10 Social Science, Gujarati medium, Chapters 2 and 4, pp. 15 and 31; Gujarati Vishwakosh, entries Rasa/Raso, Akhyan, Pad, Garbi-Garbo, Fatana, Marasiya, Khandakavya, Sonnet, Kant and Thakore, Balwantray Kalyanray; Jhaverchand Meghani, Ritugeeto, section Mitravirahana Marashiya; Amarkathao, Gujarati Lagna Geet Fatana Collection, entry Gharma Noti Khand.
